summary.title: ICPAC — All Ethiopia
summary.text: Category agreement of 54.8% within the compared area, which covers 59% of the analysed national area. Predominant category in both: above normal. Periods differ (Mar 2026–May 2026 vs Feb 2026–May 2026).

summary.title: ICPAC — FMAM rainfall domain (FMAM >= 20% of annual and >= 100 mm)
summary.text: Category agreement of 55.0% within the compared area, which covers 72% of the analysed domain. Predominant category in both: above normal. Periods differ (Mar 2026–May 2026 vs Feb 2026–May 2026).

summary.title: EMI — whole zones
summary.text: Platform area mean of local probabilities over each EMI zone, below / near / above: zone West: no clear category in one source, platform 32% / 33% / 35%; zone North-central: no clear category in one source, platform 26% / 35% / 39%; zone South-central: both favour above normal, platform 22% / 33% / 45%; zone Southeast: both favour above normal, platform 20% / 32% / 48%. summary.title: Robustness of the extraction
summary.text: With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the All Ethiopia category agreement stays between 53.7% and 55.6%. With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the FMAM rainfall domain (FMAM >= 20% of annual and >= 100 mm) category agreement stays between 53.7% and 55.6%. These are bounded sensitivity checks of the extraction, not statistical confidence intervals; exact EMI zone comparisons remain unavailable.

paragraphs.text: The platform does not show a unique favoured category over EMI zone West under its applicable rule. EMI prints 25% / 30% / 45% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 32% / 33% / 35%: no clear category in one source.

The platform does not show a unique favoured category over EMI zone North-central under its applicable rule. EMI prints 10% / 30% / 60% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 26% / 35% / 39%: no clear category in one source.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions over EMI zone South-central. EMI prints 15% / 30% / 55% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 22% / 33% / 45%: same category.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions over EMI zone Southeast. EMI prints 20% / 35% / 45% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 20% / 32% / 48%: same category.

The EMI zones were digitized from the figure's fill colours and placed by fitting the country outline, so their boundaries are approximate; the figure states no reference period, so probability differences are not calculated.

The outlooks favour different categories over much of their shared displayed area in Ethiopia. ICPAC shows a favoured category on 89% of Ethiopia and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on 11%; where it shows one it favours above normal on 69%, most often at 40-50% and 33-40%. The platform favours above normal on 50% and below normal on 7% of Ethiopia. There is category agreement of 54.8% within the compared area, which covers 59% of the analysed national area; opposite categories (above vs below) on 11% of the compared area. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Mar 2026–May 2026 and the platform Feb 2026–May 2026 (Feb 2026 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

paragraphs.area: FMAM rainfall domain (FMAM >= 20% of annual and >= 100 mm)
paragraphs.text: The outlooks favour different categories over much of their shared displayed area in the FMAM rainfall domain (FMAM >= 20% of annual and >= 100 mm). ICPAC shows a favoured category on 100% of the FMAM rainfall domain (FMAM >= 20% of annual and >= 100 mm) and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on 0%; where it shows one it favours above normal on 67%, most often at 40-50% and 33-40%. The platform favours above normal on 64% and below normal on 1% of the FMAM rainfall domain (FMAM >= 20% of annual and >= 100 mm). There is category agreement of 55.0% within the compared area, which covers 72% of the analysed domain; opposite categories (above vs below) on 9% of the compared area. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Mar 2026–May 2026 and the platform Feb 2026–May 2026 (Feb 2026 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

Not calculated: rainfall-anomaly differences, because no official rainfall-amount anomaly product was found in the checked ICPAC and EMI products; which forecast is more accurate, because that needs observations and a separate verification design (see Verification); same-event probability differences, because the target windows or spatial supports differ and ICPAC publishes only favoured-category intervals.

notes: Single season: descriptive scores for one year, not evidence of general skill.
Each outlook is scored against observations for its own target window; the observed tercile uses CHIRPS 1993-2025 terciles per 0.25° cell (official reference periods are not stated).
Favoured category: the leading tercile where it reaches 40% (the map display rule). "Chance" is the climatological probability of the favoured category over the same cells (about one in three).
RPSS: ranked probability skill score against the CHIRPS climatology, on identical cells; ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its interval, so no RPSS is computed for ICPAC.
EMI zone probabilities are applied uniformly over each digitized zone.

windows.Mar 2026, Apr 2026, May 2026: sum of verified monthly totals (Mar, Apr, May); terciles from the same months 1993-2025
